This notebook integrates information for species with available observed
sensitivity data. Specifically, it:

-   Builds a phylogeny tree from the Open Tree of Life

-   Matches species to body mass data (species level, or genus fallback
    if missing)

-   Assigns functional groups (resource groups for algae, functional
    feeding groups for invertebrate, trophic guilds for fish)

The output is a combined dataset with species' taxonomy, phylogeny, body
mass, and assigned functional groups.

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
rm(list=ls())
library(here)
library(tidyverse)  
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(rotl)
library(ape)
library(ggtree)
library(ggtreeExtra)
library(ggnewscale)
library(data.table)

options(dplyr.summarise.inform = FALSE)
```

# 1. Load dataset

Read the dataset compiled from step
1_compile_observed_sensitivity_data.rmd.

```{r}
combined_observed_sensitivity <- readRDS(here("data/1_observed_sensitivity/combined_observed_sensitivity/combined_observed_sensitivity.rds"))

spe_tax_uni <- combined_observed_sensitivity %>%
  select(latin, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus) %>%
  distinct() 
```

```{r}
# species composisiton in the 1546 species with observed sensitivity data
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)

# Normalize and define groups
algae_phyla <- c(
  "chlorophyta","charophyta","rhodophyta","ochrophyta",
  "haptophyta","cryptophyta","cyanobacteria","myzozoa","euglenozoa"
)

fish_classes <- c("actinopterygii","petromyzonti","elasmobranchii",
                  "chondrichthyes","myxini","hyperoartia","sarcopterygii")

crustacean_classes <- c("malacostraca","branchiopoda","copepoda",
                        "ostracoda","maxillopoda","thecostraca","hexanauplia",
                        "remipedia","cephalocarida")

classified <- spe_tax_uni %>%
  mutate(across(c(kingdom, phylum, class),
                ~ tolower(as.character(.x)))) %>%
  distinct(latin, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    group = case_when(
      !is.na(phylum) & phylum %in% algae_phyla           ~ "algae",
      !is.na(class)  & class  %in% fish_classes          ~ "fish",
      !is.na(class)  & class  %in% crustacean_classes    ~ "crust inv",
      TRUE                                               ~ "non-crust inv"
    )
  )

sum(classified$group %in% c("algae","fish") & classified$source != "adore")

# Counts + proportions
counts <- classified %>%
  count(group, name = "n_species") %>%
  mutate(prop = n_species / sum(n_species)) %>%
  arrange(factor(group, levels = c("algae","crust inv","non-crust inv","fish")))

counts

lvl <- counts$group
plot_df <- counts %>%
  dplyr::mutate(group = factor(group, levels = lvl))

ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = group, y = prop)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(n_species, " (", percent(prop, accuracy = 0.1), ")")),
            vjust = -0.5, size = 6) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "") +
  theme_void(base_size = 20) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 15, hjust = 0.6),  
    plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10)                
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off")  

non_crust_in_adore <- classified %>%
  filter(tolower(source) == "adore", group == "non-crust inv") %>%
  select(latin, group, kingdom, phylum, class) %>%
  arrange(group, phylum, class, latin)

```


# 2. Correct species names

Here we:

-   Remove unresolved names (e.g. “sp.” or “spp.”).

-   Drop taxa above genus level.

-   Apply corrections for known mis-spelled or outdated names.

-   Assign each taxon to a broad ecological group (Algae, Invertebrate,
    Vertebrate).

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# filter out species with sp. spp. as these species cannot be included in the phylogeny tree
# filter out species at higher than genus level
spe_tax_clean <- spe_tax_uni %>%
  filter(!grepl("\\bsp\\.?\\b|\\bspp\\.?\\b", latin, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(genus)) %>%
  mutate(
    latin = case_when(
      latin == "lithodes antarcticus" ~ "lithodes antarctica",
      latin == "Viviparus bengalensis" ~ "filopaludina bengalensis",
      latin == "acanthomysis sculpta" ~ "holmesimysis sculpta",
      latin == "acartia clausi" ~ "acartia clausii",
      latin == "acartia lillgeborgi" ~ "acartia lilljeborgii",
      latin == "acheilognathus moriokae" ~ "acheilognathus melanogaster",
      latin == "achnanthes minutissima" ~ "achnanthidium minutissimum",
      latin == "nuria danrica" ~ "esomus danrica",
      latin == "oreochromis mossambicus x urolepis" ~ "oreochromis mossambicus",
      latin == "oreochromis mossambicus x niloticus" ~ "oreochromis mossambicus", 
      latin == "enteromorpha intestinalis" ~ "ulva intestinalis", 
      TRUE ~ latin   
    )
  ) %>% distinct()

spe_tax_clean <- spe_tax_clean %>%
  mutate(group = case_when(
    phylum %in% c("charophyta","chlorophyta","cryptophyta","cyanobacteria",
                  "euglenozoa","haptophyta","myzozoa","ochrophyta","rhodophyta") ~ "Algae",
    phylum %in% c("annelida","arthropoda","mollusca","nematoda","platyhelminthes") ~ "Invertebrate",
    phylum %in% c("chordata") ~ "Vertebrate",
    TRUE ~ "Other"
  ))
```

Summary:

```{r}
length(unique(spe_tax_clean$latin))
table(spe_tax_clean$group)

```

# 3. Build phylogeny tree

We build a phylogeny tree using the Open Tree of Life. We standardize
branch lengths using Grafen’s method and filter our dataset to only
species present in the tree.

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
tx_search <- tnrs_match_names(spe_tax_clean$latin, context_name = "All life")
ott_ids <- ott_id(tx_search)
# ott_in_tree <- ott_ids[is_in_tree(ott_ids)]
# saveRDS(ott_in_tree, file = here("data/phylogeny/ott_in_tree.rds"))

ott_in_tree <- readRDS(here("data/3_phylogeny/ott_in_tree.rds"))
tree <- tol_induced_subtree(ott_ids = ott_in_tree)
tree$tip.label <- tolower(tx_search$search_string[match(
    as.numeric(gsub(".*_ott", "", tree$tip.label)),
    tx_search$ott_id
  )]) # use the original latin names in the phylogeny tree
tree <- compute.brlen(tree, method = "Grafen")

species_in_tree <- tree$tip.label
n_species_in_tree <- length(species_in_tree)

spe_tax_clean_tree <- spe_tax_clean %>%
  filter(tolower(latin) %in% species_in_tree)
```

# 4. Match body mass

We add each species with body mass estimates from a curated literature
database. The matching proceeds in two steps:

-   Species level: exact match on species name.

-   Genus level fallback: if species data are missing, we assign the
    genus average.

```{r}
sp_BM <- readRDS(here("data/4_body_mass/BM_species_summary.rds")) %>%
  mutate(
    latin = tolower(latin),
    genus = tolower(genus)
  ) %>%
  rename(BMsource = sources)

spe_tax_sub <- spe_tax_clean_tree %>%
  mutate(
    latin = tolower(latin),
    genus = tolower(genus))

n_species_total <- n_distinct(spe_tax_sub$latin)

# Species-level match
species_match <- spe_tax_sub %>%
  left_join(sp_BM %>% select(latin, mean_mass_g, BMsource), by = "latin") %>%
  mutate(BM_match_level = ifelse(!is.na(mean_mass_g), "species", NA))

n_species_match <- n_distinct(species_match$latin[species_match$BM_match_level == "species"])

# Genus-level fallback for unmatched
# Compute genus average mass from sp_BM
genus_avg <- sp_BM %>%
  group_by(genus) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_mass_g_genus = mean(mean_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE),
    BMsource = paste(unique(BMsource), collapse = "; "), 
    .groups = "drop"
  )

genus_match <- species_match %>%
  filter(is.na(mean_mass_g)) %>%     
  select(-BMsource) %>%
  left_join(genus_avg, by = "genus") %>%
  mutate(
    mean_mass_g = mean_mass_g_genus,
    BM_match_level = ifelse(!is.na(mean_mass_g_genus), "genus", "unmatched")
  ) %>%
  select(-mean_mass_g_genus)

n_genus_match <- n_distinct(genus_match$latin[genus_match$BM_match_level == "genus"])

final_match <- bind_rows(
  species_match %>% filter(BM_match_level == "species"),
  genus_match
) %>%
  distinct(latin, .keep_all = TRUE)

match_summary <- tibble(
  total_species = n_species_total,
  species_level = n_species_match,
  genus_level   = n_genus_match,
  unmatched     = n_species_total - n_species_match - n_genus_match
)

kable(match_summary)

```

Correct species with known body mass errors
```{r}
spe_mass <- final_match %>%
  filter(BM_match_level != "unmatched") 

spe_mass <- spe_mass %>%
  mutate(
    mean_mass_g = case_when(
      str_to_lower(latin) == "nitzschia closterium"      ~ 1.58e-09, #use genus level mass
      str_to_lower(latin) == "neanthes arenaceodentata"   ~ 0.0147, #DOI: 10.1002/tox.1021
      str_to_lower(latin) == "lysmata seticaudata"       ~ 0.77, #https://doi.org/10.1007/BF00404744
      str_to_lower(latin) == "odontesthes argentinensis"  ~ 92.5, #  10.3856/vol48-issue3-fulltext-2371
      str_to_lower(latin) %in% c("oryzias melastigma",
                                 "oryzias dancena",
                                 "oryzias sinensis")      ~ 1.73, # https://doi.org/10.1007/s10695-025-01548-1
      str_to_lower(latin) == "pagrus major"               ~ 104.9, #34, Bull. Eur. Ass. Fish Pathol., 32(1) 2012
      TRUE ~ mean_mass_g
    ),
    log_mass = log10(mean_mass_g)
  )
```

Remove Ulva species with weird large body mass
```{r}
length(unique(spe_mass$latin))
spe_mass <- spe_mass |> filter(!grepl("ulva", latin)) # exclude 2 species
length(unique(spe_mass$latin))
```

The composition of the species with available body mass:

```{r}
table(spe_mass$kingdom)
table(spe_mass$phylum)
table(spe_mass$group)
```

# 5. Assign functional groups

We classify species into ecological functional groups:

-   Algae → resource groups (Cyanobacteria, Diatoms, Green algae, and
    other algae)

-   Invertebrates → functional feeding groups (Filterer, Shredder,
    Gatherer, Herbivore, Predator)

-   Fish → trophic guilds (Herbivore, Detritivore, Invertivore,
    Omnivore, Piscivore, Planktivore)

```{r}
# current species with BM and phylogeny
spe_mass_temp <- spe_mass %>%
  select(latin, mean_mass_g, BMsource, BM_match_level)
length(unique(spe_mass_temp$latin))

spe_tax_clean_tree_BM <- left_join(spe_tax_clean_tree, spe_mass_temp, by = "latin") %>%
  filter(! is.na(mean_mass_g))
length(unique(spe_tax_clean_tree_BM$latin))
```

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
algae_FG <- read_csv(here("data/5_FFG/algae_FG_alina.csv")) %>%
  mutate(FG_source = "Alina")

invert_vert_FG <- read_csv(here("data/5_FFG/invert_vert_FG.csv")) %>%
  mutate(algae.tax.group = NA_character_)

FG_temp <- bind_rows(algae_FG, invert_vert_FG)

spe_tax_phylo_BM_FFG <- left_join(spe_tax_clean_tree_BM, FG_temp, by = "latin") %>%
  filter(! is.na(FG)) %>%
  filter(FG != "Unknown") 

length(unique(spe_tax_phylo_BM_FFG$latin))

table(spe_tax_phylo_BM_FFG$FG)

```

Algae fine-scale functional groups are merged into broader categories to
address limited sample sizes. 
We exclude group Parasitic as just 1 species.
For vertebrate, we combine Detritivore /
Herbivore as one group.
```{r}
spe_tax_phylo_BM_FFG$algae.group.2 <- dplyr::recode(spe_tax_phylo_BM_FFG$algae.tax.group,
  "Blue-green"      = "Cyanobacteria",
  "Green"           = "Green algae",
  "Charophytes"     = "Green algae",
  "Euglenoids"      = "Green algae",
  "Diatoms"         = "Diatom",
  "Chrysophytes"    = "Other algae",
  "Cryptomonads"    = "Other algae",
  "Dinoflagellates" = "Other algae",
  "Haptophytes"     = "Other algae",
  "Stramenopiles"   = "Other algae"
)

spe_tax_phylo_BM_FFG <- spe_tax_phylo_BM_FFG %>%
  mutate(FG2 = if_else(group == "Algae", algae.group.2, FG)) %>%
  filter(FG != "Parasitic")

```

# 6. Prune tree

The phylogenetic tree is pruned to include only species with all available information.

```{r}
splist <- unique(spe_tax_phylo_BM_FFG$latin)

# prune the tree to only include species in splist
phylo_tree <- keep.tip(tree, intersect(tree$tip.label, splist))
```

# 7. Save outputs

```{r}
# save the combined data for species
saveRDS(spe_tax_phylo_BM_FFG, file=here("data/6_combined/spe_tax_phylo_BM_FFG.rds"))

# save the tree
saveRDS(phylo_tree, file = here("data/6_combined/phylo_tree.rds"))
```



```{r}
# plot composiiton
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(forcats)
library(scales)

# Define class buckets
fish_classes <- c("actinopterygii","elasmobranchii","petromyzonti")
crustacean_classes <- c("malacostraca","branchiopoda","copepoda",
                        "ostracoda","maxillopoda","thecostraca","hexanauplia","remipedia","cephalocarida")

plot_df <- spe_tax_phylo_BM_FFG %>%
  mutate(
    group_base = tolower(group),
    class = tolower(class),
    new_group = case_when(
      group_base == "algae" ~ "algae",
      group_base == "vertebrate" & !is.na(class) & class %in% fish_classes ~ "fish",
      group_base == "invertebrate" & !is.na(class) & class %in% crustacean_classes ~ "crust inv",
      group_base == "invertebrate" ~ "non-crust inv",
      TRUE ~ "non-crust inv"           # fallback for odd cases/NA
    )
  ) %>%
  distinct(latin, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%      # one row per species
  count(new_group, name = "n_species") %>%
  mutate(prop = n_species / sum(n_species)) %>%
  mutate(new_group = factor(new_group,
                            levels = c("algae","crust inv","non-crust inv","fish")))

# Plot: proportions with "count (percent)" on bars
ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = new_group, y = prop)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(n_species, " (", percent(prop, accuracy = 0.1), ")")),
            vjust = -0.5, size = 6) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "") +
  theme_void(base_size = 20) +
   theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 15, hjust = 0.6),  
    plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10)                
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") 


```
